title: Why you won't find good startup ideas: build and the ideas find you
summary: Marc argues good startup ideas aren't discovered by searching; they emerge by accident from creating. Founders should play with new tech, solve their own problems, or listen to customers, and put work out there. His own business chain (MakeLanding to ShipFast to ZenVoice to PoopUp) was accidental.

principles.text: Good ideas can't be found by searching; successful startups are born by accident while you create.
principles.quote: Successful startups are born by accident too.

principles.text: Ideas come from playing with new tech, solving your own problem, or listening to customers.
principles.quote: It starts with the founder either playing with new technology, solving a problem they have, or listening to what their customers want.

principles.text: You don't need a good idea to start; start with small output like an article, a rebuild, or a cold email.
principles.quote: You don’t need a good idea to start. Write an article about what you learned last year, rebuild your note-taking app, or send a cold email to a business.

principles.text: Creating surfaces real problems people will pay to solve, so act rather than overthink.
principles.quote: The process of creating will help you discover problems.

principles.text: Prefer doing over thinking when looking for ideas.
One project leads to the next; his own startups chained accidentally from playing with AI.
principles.quote: My solopreneur journey was an accident. I was bored so I played with AI and created MakeLanding. MakeLanding created ShipFast.
